findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the served-streak increment mechanism: which component increments it, at what point relative to the guard's arm-2 check and the downstream record_executed reset, so the 'full window of consecutive zero-execution calls' boundary is unambiguous.
evidence: record_executed is called by the MEMO layer, which runs AFTER the outermost guard's arm-2 check for the same call (agent_call.py:266 guard body precedes descent into wrapped memo)
Plan says served paths 'extend' the streak and executed paths 'reset' it, but names no component that performs the increment
findings.finding: The mechanism never specifies WHERE or HOW the served-streak is incremented. The guard is outermost and checks arm 2 'at call entry, before increment', but at that point the downstream memo layer has not yet decided whether this call will be served (no record) or executed (record_executed resets). The plan states only that executed paths reset the streak and served paths extend it, leaving the increment site and its ordering relative to the downstream reset implicit.
findings.location: Approach paragraph — 'a served-streak backstop ... after a FULL window of consecutive zero-execution calls (checked at call entry, before increment)' and 'Cache-served paths never record, so only they can extend the served-streak'
scenarios: Implementer increments the streak inside the guard on every observation and resets via record_executed downstream — but the interleaving (increment-before-descent vs reset-during-descent) is unstated, risking an off-by-one where a call that turns out to be executed still counts toward arm 2's full-window trip
